quest.title: Vimana Agama: Royinjan's Chapter
quest.description: To find the Amiti Device to open the Ruin Golem, you decided to follow Royinjan to a secret base in Vimara Village.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x300, Primogem x40, Mora x30000, Hero's Wit x3

dialogues.speaker: Royinjan
dialogues.text: It should be in a cave somewhere near here. Is my memory going or something?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Why don't we ask the villagers of Vimara Village? They should know if there's a cave around here.

dialogues.speaker: Royinjan
dialogues.text: The villagers? Eh, there's no point asking them. This is a secret base! How would they even know where it is? If I remember correctly, the cave entrance should be behind these vines, so let's split up and search for it.

dialogues.speaker: Royinjan
dialogues.text: This great researcher and I will go look over there. You two search this place, alright?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alrighty, then let's start our search from the vines here. Gah, there really are so many of them, though...

dialogues.speaker: Ararycan
dialogues.text: These are not vines, they're Vamadha.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh? You know something about this, Ararycan?

dialogues.speaker: Ararycan
dialogues.text: Yeah, these are Vamadha. Aranara made them.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Why would the Aranara make this?

dialogues.speaker: Ararycan
dialogues.text: Aranara make Vamadha when they don't want Nara to enter a place. Where Vamadha are present, only Aranara can enter.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh... Aranara are pretty small, but the place's been blocked completely. Paimon thinks even you can't get through.

dialogues.speaker: Ararycan
dialogues.text: Nara can't get in, but Aranara can sing. Vamadha spin when they hear us singing, and when they do, we can enter.

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: #Yep! Nara {NICKNAME} is a friend of the forest. If you sing, Nara {NICKNAME}, the Vamadha will hear it. Come on, Ararycan will teach you!

dialogues.speaker: Royinjan
dialogues.text: I recall it should be around here...

dialogues.speaker: Royinjan
dialogues.text: Why can't I find it...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, no kidding! It really started spinning like a ball.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Aaand there's our mysterious cave entrance.

dialogues.speaker: Ararycan
dialogues.text: Ararycan remembers this cave.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh? Did you make this Vamadha, Ararycan?

dialogues.speaker: Ararycan
dialogues.text: Ararycan doesn't remember, but little Nara must be protected. This much Ararycan knows.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, we've no clue why this place was sealed by the Aranara, but this should be the entrance to the secret base, so let's call those two over.

dialogues.speaker: Royinjan
dialogues.text: Haha, I knew this was the place! Our secret base should be this way... How did you guys find it?

dialogues.speaker: Ararycan
dialogues.text: Ararycan did a great job.

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: Eh, either way... Since you found the entrance to the cave, let's go in. We just have to find the Amiti Device next...

dialogues.speaker: Royinjan
dialogues.text: It's pretty big inside. Don't get scared now...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow! This place is really huge! You were a pretty impressive kid, eh, Royinjan?

dialogues.speaker: Royinjan
dialogues.text: Not bad, eh? But it's much smaller than I remember.

response.speaker: Royinjan
response.text: Haha, more than grown up. I'm an old man now.

response.speaker: Royinjan
response.text: But this place really hasn't changed at all. It's like time stood still here.

response.speaker: Royinjan
response.text: Even the air smells the same. A single whiff brings back so many memories...

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: Let's not waste time. Do you remember where the Amiti Device is?

response.speaker: Royinjan
response.text: Patience, youngster. Let's take a look around first.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: One thing has been bugging Paimon since we first walked in. What is this huge machine part?

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: Oh, Ararycan knows. This was moved here from the Giant Iron Mountain.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Giant Iron Mountain... You mean it was taken from the Ruin Golem from before?

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: You noticed it too? Judging from the pattern, such parts should belong to the Ruin Golem, though I don't know why it was arranged in this fashion.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: Perhaps you really do have some academic talent. Would you like me to recommend you to study in the Akademiya once our project comes to a close?

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: You're sure to make lots of friends there.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, that's not what this is about... but thanks anyway.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But a child shouldn't have been able to move anything this big. So who piled it up here in this way?

response.speaker: Royinjan
response.text: Maybe it was a forest spirit! ...Nah, just kidding. I can't remember.

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: Ararycan knows! Ararycan moved it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: How did you move something this big?

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: Ararycan can move it. Ararycan is very strong.

response.speaker: Royinjan
response.text: Haha, I remember two groups of us kids running around this big guy and play-fighting.

choices.text: Were there that many children here before?

response.speaker: Royinjan
response.text: In the beginning, yes... Our group's stronghold should be up ahead...

response.speaker: Royinjan
response.text: Oh, I remember now. I think I buried something over there. I'll take you.

choices.text: So who won in the end?

response.speaker: Royinjan
response.text: Me, of course! I've never lost! Our group's stronghold should be up ahead...

choices.text: This is probably because Paimon's small.

response.speaker: Royinjan
response.text: I was also a child at that time. I'm an old man now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: C'mon, c'mon! Paimon wants to see what we've got... Eh? It's just a booklet.

dialogues.speaker: Royinjan
dialogues.text: Oooh, this is good stuff! This was our "Adventure Handbook" back in the day.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Adventure Handbook?

dialogues.speaker: Royinjan
dialogues.text: Don't you guys know about Adventure Handbooks? I thought you were adventurers from abroad based on how you look and the fact that you're here looking for treasure or something.

choices.text: Yes, I did in fact get an Adventurer Handbook.

response.speaker: Royinjan
response.text: Right? Many adventurers write them. It's like an adventure journal, to record their experiences, plans, and even the clues to treasure locations.

response.speaker: Royinjan
response.text: As you guys know, my grandfather was a great adventurer, though I didn't understand a lick of what he wrote into his adventure journal.

response.speaker: Royinjan
response.text: Still, I grew up wanting to be an adventurer, so I made my own imitation adventure handbook. You could say that's where I got my start.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: I know how important this is to you, but it won't help us find the thing we're looking for.

response.speaker: Royinjan
response.text: Now, now, not so fast. Didn't I tell you that I planned to find the Amiti Device? What happened then is recorded in this Adventure Handbook.

response.speaker: Royinjan
response.text: Let me see... I remember that the two of us... Wait a moment. Why are there three people in the drawing? Has my memory already gone that bad? Or is it because my eyes can't see well anymore?

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: Do you need me to lend you my glasses? I have the latest model, as produced by the Akademiya.

response.speaker: Royinjan
response.text: Sir Researcher, are you really that... Forget it, let me take a closer look... I'm pretty sure now that the Amiti Device should have been buried right here by yours truly.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: Great! So we just have to search this cave... is what I would say, if this place wasn't quite so big.

response.speaker: Royinjan
response.text: There's no need for that. The location of the device is recorded here. It should be...

choices.text: Oh, I've seen this sort of adventure log before...

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: Yes, this is indeed the Amiti Device.

dialogues.speaker: Royinjan
dialogues.text: See? I didn't lie to you guys!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yay! Now we can scuttle right back and open that giant robot up, right? Hehe, Paimon's getting excited already!

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: Hmm. Alas, this is just a fragment. There's no way we will open the Ruin Golem without a complete device.

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: I can fix it if it's not been completely destroyed, but we will have to find some way to recover the remaining pieces.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: And as for these remaining fragments...

dialogues.speaker: Royinjan
dialogues.text: Oh, don't be so anxious. The device was split into three parts.

dialogues.speaker: Royinjan
dialogues.text: But why would grandpa put them in three different locations...? You know what? This would be a very exciting story, if only I remembered more of it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Three different places... So, are the locations of the fragments recorded here?

dialogues.speaker: Royinjan
dialogues.text: Yes, that's right. The locations of the buried device fragments are all recorded in this handbook. We must have found the fragment buried here back then from... wherever it was at first.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #In that case, let's go find the remaining two fragments using this. We're the best at finding things, aren't we, {NICKNAME}?

choices.text: We're pretty good at finding things. But as for people...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #...Mm, yeah, Paimon knows what you mean. It's alright, though! We'll surely find {F#him}{M#her}.

response.speaker: Royinjan
response.text: Heh. That's what I said, anyway, but...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But?

response.speaker: Royinjan
response.text: I can't understand these writings.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh? How can that be? Didn't you write these notes yourself?

response.speaker: Royinjan
response.text: Um... Well, this is actually a record of the adventure that the two... Well, maybe the three of us undertook.

response.speaker: Royinjan
response.text: I can't remember who this third person was, but I certainly haven't forgotten that old man. If you want to know the location of the remaining device fragments, you should go look for him.

response.speaker: Royinjan
response.text: That old man should still be kicking even now, and if he is, he definitely still lives in Vimara Village. He did say he would live out the rest of his days there, after all.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: The old man you're talking about is...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Amadhiah, maybe?

response.speaker: Royinjan
response.text: Oh? You know that old fellow? Well, that makes things easier! Take this handbook and show it to him. He should understand.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh? You aren't gonna come with us?

response.speaker: Royinjan
response.text: Hmph, I don't want to meet that old fossil.

response.speaker: Royinjan
response.text: If you've figured out where the fragments are buried, go look for them yourself. I would like to go with you, but my old bones aren't up to the task anymore.

response.speaker: Royinjan
response.text: I wanted to be a great adventurer like my grandfather back when I was a young boy. And if it hadn't been for that guy...

response.speaker: Royinjan
response.text: ...Well. Stories are, in the end, more important than the adventure itself. So if you collect any stories, please remember to bring them to me.

response.speaker: Royinjan
response.text: I can give you guys this device fragment as a reward. How about that? It's a good deal, right?

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: Well, it looks like I won't be of much help in this endeavor. So I might as well wait here for you. There are a lot of parts here to study, and I'm not going to pass up the chance to do it.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: I'm counting on you two to bring the fragments back as quickly as you can. Things will get dicey for me if I miss the deadline.

choices.text: It's not like we have any other options.

dialogues.speaker: Amadhiah
dialogues.text: Ah, we meet again, friends of Rana. Is she not with you? I wonder what's taking her so long to patrol the woods this time...

dialogues.speaker: Amadhiah
dialogues.text: Still, this must be a special occasion, for you to come to see me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, yeah. It's for...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You tell Amadhiah about Royinjan, the secret base, and the handbook.\nIt is a story with a lot of twists.

dialogues.speaker: Amadhiah
dialogues.text: So you went to the secret base. What do you think? Pretty impressive, isn't it?

dialogues.speaker: Amadhiah
dialogues.text: Royinjan is here in Vimara and still doesn't want to see me. That fellow gets more stubborn the older he gets...

dialogues.speaker: Amadhiah
dialogues.text: That's how he is, though. It's almost been ten years since I last saw him.

dialogues.speaker: Amadhiah
dialogues.text: And that was when I had some business in Port Ormos. I'm relieved to hear he's still himself.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That's an odd relationship you have between you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So why doesn't Royinjan want to see you?

dialogues.speaker: Amadhiah
dialogues.text: It's a long story... You wouldn't mind hearing an old man prattle on, would you?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yes, Paimon wants to know too!

response.speaker: Amadhiah
response.text: Back when we were kids, Royinjan lived in Vimara for a while because of his grandfather.

response.speaker: Amadhiah
response.text: As a kid from bustling Port Ormos with a legendary adventurer for his grandfather, Royinjan quickly drew the attention of the other kids.

response.speaker: Amadhiah
response.text: I was one of those kids who was fascinated by the stories he heard from his grandfather.

response.speaker: Amadhiah
response.text: Together, we built a "secret base" in a cave and dressed ourselves up as warriors and heroes with branches and flowers.

response.speaker: Amadhiah
response.text: To us children, the base was another world, where we went through countless imaginary adventures.

response.speaker: Amadhiah
response.text: Those old times seem like a dream now.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Royinjan also mentioned that the base once played host to loads of kids, so what happened?

response.speaker: Amadhiah
response.text: Yeah, kids do have short attention spans in any case. Be it legends or adventures, these are just some of their many passing interests.

response.speaker: Amadhiah
response.text: By the time we realized that truth, Royinjan and I were the only two left in the base... No, make that three, actually.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Royinjan also mentioned there were three of you, but he can't recall the third person anymore.

response.speaker: Amadhiah
response.text: I'm not sure, either. It's been so long and we're both old now... Who could it have been...?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: An Aranara, perhaps?

response.speaker: Amadhiah
response.text: These "Aranara" again? Now that sounds like make-believe worthy of children.

response.speaker: Amadhiah
response.text: If I had left Vimara with him, I'd probably still believe in all that.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: With him, you say... So why did Royinjan leave then?

response.speaker: Amadhiah
response.text: For his adventures, of course. That guy's been stubborn ever since we were kids.

response.speaker: Amadhiah
response.text: We'd vowed to become the greatest adventurers in the world, just like his legendary grandfather.

response.speaker: Amadhiah
response.text: But neither of us had the knack for being one. After my initial enthusiasm had worn off, I found that I had far more important things to do.

response.speaker: Amadhiah
response.text: So in the end, he was the last one left.

response.speaker: Amadhiah
response.text: That's why we're like this now. The way he sees it, I was more of an adventurer, yet I gave up before he did.

response.speaker: Amadhiah
response.text: Stubbornness, that's all it is. Still, it was also thanks to Royinjan's stubbornness that he wound up being the best antique dealer in Port Ormos.

response.speaker: Amadhiah
response.text: Well, that's it for the story. You want to know where to find the two fragments, right?

response.speaker: Amadhiah
response.text: It's going to take a while to mark them out for you, though. My eyesight's gotten quite deplorable in my old age...

response.speaker: Amadhiah
response.text: I'll count this as a commission from him. I used traditional Vimara cursive for this, which he should be able to comprehend — he definitely would've back then, anyway!

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Amadhiah makes some notes about the fragments, using the handbook as a reference.

response.speaker: Amadhiah
response.text: It's done. Just follow the instructions and you'll be all right. To be honest, I never thought that this thing would still have its uses after all these years.

response.speaker: Amadhiah
response.text: Ah, yes, I just found this in the journal too.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Grandpa Amadhiah picks a dried flower out from the yellowed sheets.

response.speaker: Amadhiah
response.text: Give this to Royinjan when you see him again. Maybe this will jog his memory a bit.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Why didn't you say anything back there, Ararycan? Amadhiah's a good Nara. You have nothing to fear.

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: Ararycan wasn't afraid. Ararycan has heard of the things you talked about earlier, and they're very familiar. Just can't remember them...

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: Ararycan was confused, so Ararycan didn't say anything.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: That's quite a strange problem, Ararycan.

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: Yes, very strange!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: This is tiring, but at least we're making progress. Anyway, let's do what Amadhiah said and go find the two fragments, then give them to Jazari.

choices.text: As long as you don't go on for too long...

response.speaker: Amadhiah
response.text: Ha, I'll make it short!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey Royinjan, we're back!

dialogues.speaker: Royinjan
dialogues.text: There you are. Looks like you met the old man and found the fragments you were looking for, hmm?

dialogues.speaker: Royinjan
dialogues.text: That aside, is he as tedious now as he was then? Not that I care though.

response.speaker: Royinjan
response.text: What did Amadhiah tell you? Don't believe anything he said! If he hadn't slipped back into the village the night before our adventure at sea...

response.speaker: Royinjan
response.text: We could have been the greatest adventurers in history.

response.speaker: Royinjan
response.text: Come on, I'm just kidding. I'm better suited to dealing in antiques.

response.speaker: Royinjan
response.text: Even a great adventurer like my grandfather eventually went missing in their adventures. I doubt I would've stood much of a chance.

response.speaker: Royinjan
response.text: For me, I'd be satisfied so long as there's a story to hear. So, what stories have you collected? According to our deal, the device fragments in your hands were meant to be exchanged for stories.

choices.text: About the inundated device and The Withering...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You tell Royinjan about your search for the device fragments.

response.speaker: Royinjan
response.text: Haha, that's a great adventure indeed. You are marvelous adventurers. If only I had been able to complete such a journey myself.

response.speaker: Royinjan
response.text: That's a good enough story for me. The fragments are yours, as we agreed.

response.speaker: Royinjan
response.text: Take them to our great researcher. He's been stressing out this entire time while you were out having your fun.

response.speaker: Royinjan
response.text: I should get back to my shop now. I'll be quite upset if I missed out on a big sale.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait a second, we have something else we have to do. That flower...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Amadhiah wanted you to have this.

response.speaker: Royinjan
response.text: A flower? Seriously? At his age?

response.speaker: Royinjan
response.text: Hold on, I think I remember this...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Have you recalled anything?

response.speaker: Royinjan
response.text: Haha. Maybe, but then again, maybe not. Anyway, the past should stay in the past, so forget it.

response.speaker: Royinjan
response.text: But I have a feeling this flower does not belong to me, so please, return it to where it belongs. I can tell that you can see things I can't.

response.speaker: Royinjan
response.text: He seems to have become a bit more fun than before...

response.speaker: Royinjan
response.text: Do drop by my shop when you get the chance. Until then, farewell!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Where it belongs... The flower is yours, Ararycan.

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: This flower is precious. Why give it to Ararycan?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Because it belongs to you!

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: Ararycan doesn't remember the flower, but Ararycan likes it.

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: Ararycan cherishes this flower. Ararycan shall plant it in the garden.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We'll see you at the foot of the Great Iron Mountain. Once we get the giant machine started, we'll go get the bad guys together.

response.speaker: Ararycan
response.text: Yes, Ararycan wants to fight the bad guys with you!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's a promise, Ararycan!

choices.text: About the fairies and the children...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You tell Royinjan about the adventure of the Aranara and the children.

response.speaker: Royinjan
response.text: Fairies in the forest... I've heard similar legends before, but your tale is a particularly interesting one.

talks.objective: Talk to Royinjan in the secret base

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: Thank goodness you're back.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Here are the two remaining fragments...

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: Ah, yes, that's them, alright! Thank you so much for your help. I'll take care of the rest.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Jazari fixes the Amiti Device.

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: Well, this should do the trick. Haha, pretty good, eh? Why, I bet that even a Herbad of the Akademiya couldn't fix this thing without consulting any information.

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: You're lucky to have me with you, you know? Now we can get inside the Ruin Golem!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Uh... I think that's our line.

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: Ah, no one's been in this machine for centuries. I can already smell the parchment of the pages in the academic annals that shall bear my name! ...Oh, um, sorry. I got too excited.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No problem. Paimon's getting excited too! Mora or treasure, here we come!

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: Ugh, why am I looking for some secret base here again...? Oh, whatever. It's all in the name of academic research. Yes, yes...

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: We're going to fall behind on research progress if we don't find the Amiti Device quickly.

dialogues.speaker: Royinjan
dialogues.text: This is such a nostalgic place. It's like the very dirt and air here are trying to tell me something... But I just can't recall anything.

dialogues.speaker: Royinjan
dialogues.text: Did you guys find the device fragments you're after? Remember to bring the stories you've collected to me afterward, alright?

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: I didn't expect that there would be a Ruin Golem component that I've never seen before. How much more of this Ruin Golem have I not discovered?

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: Have you found the fragments of the Amiti Device? My academic career is in your hands here!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Y'know, Paimon's used to this already... But why has this become a problem that only the two of us can solve again?

dialogues.speaker: Ararycan
dialogues.text: Two? You didn't count Ararycan in. Bad Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... Ararycan is Aranara, so you don't really count!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's not sure what's going on here. How about we go see Amadhiah about it?
